definitions.explanation: A colloquial, non-technical term for harmful microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens. Used in everyday conversation, especially when talking about hygiene and illness.

examples.english: Let's wash our hands so germs don't get in.

examples.japanese: ⟦{傷口|きずぐち}→傷口：09517_kizuguchi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ばい{菌|きん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{化膿|かのう}→化膿：15315_kanou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: If germs get into a wound, it will become infected.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、⟦{汚|きたな}い→汚い：00788_kitanai⟧もの⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{触|さわ}る→触る：00808_sawaru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧「ばい{菌|きん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われた→言う：00515_iu⟧ものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, if I touched dirty things, people would say 'you'll get germs.'

notes:
USAGE:
An everyday word used particularly by and when speaking to children. Not a scientific term — in technical contexts, ⟦{細菌|さいきん}→細菌：13791_saikin⟧ (bacteria), ⟦ウイルス→ウイルス：05223_uirusu⟧ (virus), or ⟦{微生物|びせいぶつ}→微生物：12665_biseibutsu⟧ (microorganism) are used instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ばい{菌|きん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (germs get in)
- ばい{菌|きん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく (germs stick to, germs spread)
- ばい{菌|きん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{殺|ころ}す→殺す：01944_korosu⟧ (to kill germs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{細菌|さいきん}→細菌：13791_saikin⟧: bacteria — the technical/scientific term
- ⟦{病原菌|びょうげんきん}→病原菌：22355_byougenkin⟧: pathogenic bacteria — medical term
- ⟦{雑菌|ざっきん}→雑菌：28516_zakkin⟧: miscellaneous bacteria — technical, used for non-specific contamination
